timeline.title: How the World Celebrates Turning One
items: The story goes that ancient Greeks lit round honey cakes with candles for Artemis, goddess of the moon.
At a first birthday called a dol, babies pick an object like a pencil or thread, said to hint at their future.
In Germany, children's birthday parties called Kinderfest brought a cake with a candle for every year.
Sisters Mildred and Patty Hill published the tune we now know as Happy Birthday to You.
today: Candles, cake and a song. And a whole family singing it just for you.

letters.title: Wise Words for Your Next Steps
items: The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Today you are You, that is truer than true.
Dr. Seuss, Happy Birthday to You!, 1959
Children are the living messages we send to a time we will not see.
Fall seven times, stand up eight.
letters.hand: Whatever step comes next, {first}, we will be right behind you.

facts.title: How Babies Learn Absolutely Everything
items: Babies learn by watching our faces and copying them. Every silly face we pulled was a lesson.
Long before real words, babies babble ba ba and da da, practising the sounds of their language.
Babies understand lots of words months before they can say a single one out loud.
Peekaboo delights babies partly because they are learning that hidden things still exist.
Most babies laugh out loud for the first time at around three or four months old.
Lots of babies take their first steps around their first birthday. Some like to take their time.
facts.hand: You learned so much this year, {first}. We watched every bit.

world.title: Why the World Is Better With You in It
world.lead: In just one year, you gave the world:
items: A giggle that makes strangers smile.
A brand new dancer, any music will do.
A wave for every bus and every dog.
Socks that somehow vanish one by one.
A family that grew a little bigger.
A whole year of tiny brilliant firsts.
And the happiest one year old we know.
world.close: The world is better because of you, {first}. Ours most of all.

note.title: What we believe a first birthday is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but this one was for someone who has only just turned one.
We believe a first birthday is really a party for a whole year: every giggle, every wobble, every first word and every sleepless night that somehow became the best year of all.
{first}, you will not remember this birthday. That is why someone wanted it kept here, so you could read it one day and see how loved you were.
That someone is {from}. From everything they told us, you made this year the happiest they have known.
note.wish: Happy first birthday, {first}. Here is to every year after.
